stated: Introduce a holistic and comprehensive National Food Strategy to ensure food security, tackle rising food prices, end food poverty and improve health and nutrition.

source.quote: Introduce a holistic and comprehensive National Food Strategy to ensure food security, tackle rising food prices, end food poverty and improve health and nutrition.

bearing_set.reason: Explicitly targets rising food prices and food poverty, both core components of the cost-of-living basket (food costs, disposable income for lower-income households).
'Improve health and nutrition' as a stated goal directly affects population health outcomes, preventable disease burden, and downstream NHS demand/capacity.
Ending food poverty is an explicit distributional objective that, if effective, would narrow the gap between the poorest and the rest on a basic-needs dimension — directly moving the inequality gap.

membership_note: The three bearings map cleanly to the policy's own stated goals: food prices → O2, health/nutrition → O3, food poverty → O14. Environmental/agricultural spillovers (O6) and public-finance costs (O12) are real possibilities but cannot be given a non-negligible verdict from the vague 'strategy' framing alone without named mechanisms or spending figures.
